newsitem.title: UK: Paper Brent spreads wider, Oct N. Sea slow to sell.
newsitem.headline: Paper Brent spreads wider, Oct N. Sea slow to sell.

text.p: Paper Brent spreads staged a recovery with the outright market on Tuesday afternoon and a slump in physical cargo differentials looked to have been stemmed.

Oct/Nov and Nov/Dec Brent spreads widened to about +52/+55 cents on a 50-cent November recovery to $22.10 a barrel. October North Sea buying from newly released programmes was taking its time to get off the ground, with a handful of cargoes still available for September loading.
But dealers said the charter by J.P. Morgan of a tanker to carry one million barrels of Brent to the U.S. Gulf had provided some encouragement for sickly differentials.
Better margins after Monday's late crude slump would also help put a floor under differentials, they said.

In the Med, refiners were showing no appetite for prompt barrels despite a marked improvement in margins, and were waiting to see what would happen to prompt barrels, including a 135,000-tonne cargo waiting to load at Novorossiisk on Sept 19.
"With the crude price falling, the extra margin you are talking about in the Med is $3 a barrel for Urals," the trader said.
"But I don't think refiners will be jumping to buy crude. Some adjustment is needed first."
Traders said it was hard to assess September values for Urals because of weather-related loading delays at the main Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk, where four ships are waiting to load.
Nigerian crude traders were waiting for the announcement of October term prices.
